verdicts.label: A
verdicts.evidence: Lumberjack can always ensure at least 4 cells in any $3 \times 3$ block don't grow by picking them every time the gardener picks the center cell. For the overall board, L can remove 4 units of height for every 9 units G adds, meaning at most 5/9 of the height is preserved. Thus, G cannot ensure all trees are majestic.

verdicts.label: B
verdicts.evidence: If the gardener picks every square on the board $m$ times, each interior tree's height increases by $9m$. The lumberjack can remove $4mN^2$ units of height. To minimize the number of majestic trees, the lumberjack will concentrate subtractions to fully eliminate as many trees as possible. The number of eliminated trees is at most $4mN^2 / 9m = 4/9 N^2$. The remaining $5/9 N^2$ trees will be majestic for large $m$. For $N=2025$, $5/9 \times 2025^2 = 2278125$.

verdicts.label: C
verdicts.evidence: $K=5$ is the result for a $3 \times 3$ board, but for a $2025 \times 2025$ board, the gardener can pick every square to increase the number of majestic trees.

verdicts.label: D
verdicts.evidence: $K=9$ is the result for a $3 \times 3$ board if the lumberjack could not remove any height. For a $2025 \times 2025$ board, the gardener can ensure many more majestic trees.
